# Migration Plan: 2 TB On-Prem PostgreSQL → Managed Cloud Database

1. **Assessment & tooling decision** — Inventory schema, extensions, roles, cron jobs, and app connection strings. Given 2 TB and a 2-hour window, select a **logical replication / CDC tool** (e.g., AWS DMS, pglogical, or native logical replication) for near-zero-downtime sync, rather than relying on dump/restore alone within the window.

2. **Provision target environment** — Stand up the managed cloud PostgreSQL instance with matching major version, required extensions, parameter/config parity, sizing, VPC/networking, and security groups. Validate connectivity from app servers.

3. **Stakeholder communication (initial)** — Notify all stakeholders and the 4,000 DAU user base (status page, email/in-app banner) of the scheduled Sunday maintenance window, expected impact, and duration, at least 3–5 days in advance.

4. **Baseline full backup (pre-rehearsal)** — Take a full verified backup of production (pg_basebackup or snapshot) before touching anything. Restore this backup into a non-production/staging copy for rehearsal — production itself is not modified.

5. **Dry run / rehearsal** — On the staging copy, execute the entire migration runbook end-to-end: initial load, replication setup, cutover script, DNS/connection-string switch, verification queries, and rollback steps. Record timings; confirm the cutover portion fits well inside the 2-hour window.

6. **Establish live replication** — Using a fresh full backup as the initial snapshot, configure logical replication/CDC from on-prem to the cloud target so it streams and catches up **before** the maintenance window opens, minimizing in-window work to just the final cutover.

7. **Go/no-go communication** — Send a final reminder to stakeholders and users 24 hours and 1 hour before the window, including the rollback contingency and a designated incident channel/on-call contact.

8. **Pre-cutover final backup & write freeze** — At the start of the maintenance window, take one last full backup/snapshot of production, then put the application into read-only/maintenance mode to stop new writes. This is the mandatory backup checkpoint immediately before any production-modifying action.

9. **Final sync & cutover** — Let replication reach zero lag, then repoint application connection strings/DNS to the cloud database, and run smoke tests (connect, basic reads/writes on a test table).

10. **Data integrity verification** — Before reopening to users, compare source vs. target: table-by-table row counts, checksums (e.g., `pg_checksums`/hash aggregates per table), max/sequence values, and index/constraint counts. Only proceed if all match within tolerance.

11. **Resume traffic & close out** — Take the application out of maintenance mode, monitor error rates/latency/replication lag closely for the remainder of the window and following hours, then send final stakeholder/user communication confirming success and closure of the window.

12. **Rollback procedure** — If verification fails or critical errors appear at any point after step 8: re-enable maintenance mode, repoint connection strings/DNS back to the (still-live, unmodified) on-prem database, restore from the pre-cutover backup (step 8) if on-prem was altered, notify stakeholders of the postponement, and retain the cloud instance for root-cause analysis before re-attempting.

STEP COUNT: 12
